title: Contract Paralegal
description:

You will support case progression, client service, and financial accuracy while contributing to continuous improvement within the team.

Responsibilities will include
- Manage fee-earning end-to-end case work and take ownership of allocated matters under supervision.

- Draft correspondence and review incoming correspondence from third parties.
- Manage key dates and deadlines accurately.
- Update the Peppermint system to ensure data capture and MI reporting are accurate.

- Support continuous improvement and change initiatives within the team.

- Experience in paralegal or fee-earning casework is desirable or a legal degree
- Strong written communication skills, including drafting correspondence.
- Good attention to detail and strong organisational skills.
- Ability to manage deadlines, key dates, and financial processes.
- Confident using case management systems and working within set procedures.

Monday - Friday 9am - 5pm

The Salary

£26,500.

3-6 months

The Location:

Central Bristol, no car parking

title: Peripatetic Service Coordinator - Mental Health
description:
Please note that the closing date for this post has been extended to 14th October to allow more time for applications.

We are looking for an experienced and compassionate leader to join our Mental Health Services as a Peripatetic Service Coordinator, supporting teams across Bristol and South Gloucestershire. This is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference to the lives of people with complex mental health needs while supporting and developing high-performing teams.

As a Service Coordinator, you will lead teams to support people with complex mental health needs to achieve their goals, build independence, and develop the skills and confidence needed to live fulfilling lives within their communities. You will help people build resilience, develop practical life skills, strengthen community connections, and take greater control of their future through person-centred support.

You will be an inspirational and supportive leader with excellent communication and listening skills, able to motivate, develop and empower colleagues to deliver outstanding support. You will have a strong understanding of person-centred practice and a commitment to promoting positive mental health, wellbeing and recovery-focused support.

You will ensure services operate safely, effectively and in line with relevant legislation, regulations and organisational standards, while evidencing positive outcomes for the people we support.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing the day-to-day operation of services, including rota planning and resource allocation, to ensure people receive the right support at the right time.
- Supporting teams to co-produce and regularly review support plans, risk assessments and positive risk management strategies.
- Providing regular supervision, coaching and performance support to team members, while ensuring training and development needs are met.
- Contributing to referrals, assessments and service transition planning.
- Monitoring service budgets and expenditure in line with organisational expectations.
- Providing direct, hands-on support when required and leading by example in delivering high-quality care and support.

The successful candidate will:
- Demonstrate strong leadership skills, with experience of supervising, leading or coordinating a team.
- Be highly organised and able to prioritise competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
- Have experience supporting people with complex mental health needs and a sound understanding of recovery-focused practice.
- Be confident in responding to people who are experiencing acute mental illness, in dynamic risk management and developing escalation plans to ensure that people receive the support that they need.
- Have knowledge of mental health services, legislation and best practice, including experience of trauma-informed approaches.
- Be flexible to work across a seven-day service, including a variety of shift patterns as required.

In return, you will have the opportunity to lead dedicated teams, shape service delivery, and support people on their recovery journey within a values-driven organisation committed to learning, inclusion and continuous improvement.

At Milestones Trust we recognise that without the hard work, commitment and passion of our staff, we wouldn't be the charity that we are today. In return, we are committed to rewarding you with a competitive pay and benefits package including:
- 34 days' annual leave, including recognised public holidays
- Learning and development to support your career growth
- Nationally recognised qualifications, from entry level care to management
- Flexible working, with rotas provided in advance
- Occupational Sick Pay after two years, increasing with service
- Health Cash Plan after probation, offering at least £695 cashback for health treatments (dental, optical, therapies, maternity/paternity, prescriptions)
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay
- Free enhanced DBS check
- Dayforce Wallet, giving you access to your earnings before payday
- Employee referral scheme with financial rewards
- Employee Assistance Programme from day one, offering confidential 24/7 support
- Company pension scheme to help grow your retirement savings

We pride ourselves with being able to offer staff opportunities to develop and progress their careers within the Trust.

title: Technical Claims Handler
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new firm

Our client is a highly respected UK law firm with a well-established insurance practice and a growing delegated claims handling service. Based in the firm's Bristol office, the team manages claims on an outsourced basis for a broad range of leading insurers, underwriting businesses and insurance organisations.

Operating under delegated authority, the team reviews, adjusts and settles claims from first notification through to resolution. Its work focuses on financial loss claims made against professionals, including professional indemnity, title indemnity, technology and media matters. The team does not handle consumer, retail or personal injury claims.

The wider claims function is structured across scheme managers, technical claims handlers, senior claims handlers and claims handlers. Each client is supported by a dedicated scheme manager and claims team, with individuals typically working across more than one client or scheme. This role will be based in the firm's Bristol office, with occasional travel to London where required.

Your new role

This opportunity is available on either a permanent or a 9 month fixed-term contract basis, offering flexibility depending on your preference and circumstances.

An excellent opportunity to join a specialist and growing team, managing a reduced caseload of complex professional indemnity claims while providing technical support, coaching and guidance to colleagues. You'll work closely with insurers, scheme managers and stakeholders to deliver high-quality claims handling and strategic decision-making.
Key responsibilities:
- Manage complex professional indemnity claims from notification to resolution.
- Assess policy coverage, liability, quantum and insurer exposure.
- Investigate claims, develop strategies and make decisions within delegated authority.
- Negotiate settlements and provide accurate insurer reporting.
- Manage external legal providers where required.
- Support, mentor and train claims colleagues.
- Build strong relationships with insurers, brokers, insureds and stakeholders.
- Ensure compliance with SLAs, KPIs and reserving requirements.
- Maintain accurate records on the case management system.

What you'll need to succeed

You will have strong technical claims handling experience and a sound understanding of insurance principles, policy coverage and delegated authority arrangements. Previous professional indemnity claims experience would be valuable, although the team is also open to candidates from transferable insurance backgrounds, including commercial insurance or legal expenses insurance, who demonstrate the right technical aptitude and attitude to learning.You will be confident assessing policy coverage, liability and quantum, and able to make well-reasoned decisions in the best interests of insurers. You will also understand the importance of compliance, accurate reporting, service level agreements and the consistent application of client reserving policies.As an important part of the role involves supporting others, you should enjoy coaching, mentoring and sharing technical knowledge with colleagues. You will be able to explain complex claims issues clearly and provide constructive guidance to less experienced team members.You will also possess:
- Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work.
- Commercial and practical approach to claims handling.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

What you'll get in return

You will join a growing and specialist claims team, gaining exposure to complex, high-quality professional indemnity work for an impressive range of insurers and delegated authority providers.The firm is prepared to invest in training candidates with relevant transferable insurance experience. You will receive technical support from experienced claims professionals, alongside specialist training delivered by lawyers from across the wider firm, including teams with expertise in areas such as construction and professional negligence.There is a strong focus on developing and promoting people internally. As the team continues to grow, there may be opportunities to progress into senior claims handling, technical supervision or scheme management positions, subject to individual development and suitable roles becoming available.The firm offers a supportive, inclusive and collaborative working environment, together with a flexible hybrid working approach where possible. Support and reasonable adjustments are available throughout the recruitment process and during employment.

What you need to do now

If you are interested in this Technical Claims Handler opportunity or would like further information, please get in touch for a confidential discussion.If this position is not quite right but you are considering new opportunities within claims, insurance or legal services, we would still be keen to hear from you.We would expect someone with the appropriate level of technical claims experience to have developed the skills required for this position. However, applications from candidates with different levels or types of relevant insurance experience are encouraged and will be considered.

Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers. By applying for this job you accept the T&C's, Privacy Policy and Disclaimers which can be found at hays.co.uk

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant
- Location: Bath
- Job Type: Part-time (22.5 hours per week)
- Salary: £30,000 p.a. pro rata

We are seeking an Accounts Assistant to join our family run business. This role is crucial in supporting the Financial Controller with a range of financial tasks including Accounts Payable (AP) and Accounts Receivable (AR) activities and general financial administration. This position is ideal for someone who is organised, reliable, and proactive, and thrives in a small, dynamic team environment.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Accounts Payable (AP): Process supplier invoices with accurate coding and approval, maintain the AP ledger, ensure timely payment runs, and reconcile supplier statements.
- Accounts Receivable (AR): Assist in checking and approving tenant invoices, be the first point of contact for credit control, maintain the AR ledger, and update tenant accounts.
- Banking & Reconciliation: Perform daily bank reconciliations, post financial entries, and manage tenant deposit accounts.
- Service Charge & Property Management Support: Assist in the reconciliations of service charge budgets, maintain property-related financial records, and liaise with property managers, suppliers, and tenants regarding finance-related queries.
- Month-End & Reporting: Prepare control account reconciliations, assist with month-end processes, and prepare reports for management and stakeholders.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Experience in an Accounts Assistant or Finance Assistant role.
- Strong understanding of Accounts Payable and/or Accounts Receivable processes.
- Excellent numerical accuracy and attention to detail.
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel.
- Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks.
- Excellent communication skills.

Desirable:
- Experience in property management or real estate finance.
- Knowledge of service charge accounting.
- Familiarity with property management or accounting software (e.g., Xero, ApprovalMax, Re-Leased).

Personal Attributes:
- Proactive and organised, comfortable with varied tasks.
- Reliable and trustworthy with strong ownership of duties.
- Inquisitive nature, actively seeking improvement opportunities.
- Collaborative with a "can-do" attitude.

Benefits:
- Competitive pro rata salary.
- Flexible working hours across 3-5 days.
- Opportunity to work in a dynamic and supportive team environment.
- Involvement in varied and impactful financial tasks.

To apply for the Accounts Assistant position, please submit your CV and cover letter detailing your relevant experience and why you are interested in this role.

title: Reception and Appointment Clerk
description: The Reception and Appointment Clerk works across a number of sites providing reception, administrative and appointment booking support for Haematology and Oncology services. The role involves booking appointments, managing telephone systems, supporting patient pathways and undertaking a range of administrative duties to ensure the smooth running of services across both Bristol and Weston. **Location - Weston General Hospital** The Reception and Appointment Clerk works closely with a wide range of administrative teams including the Treatment Bookings Team, Clinic Coordinators, Medical Secretaries and Clinical Nurse Specialist Support Team. As the team deal with a wide range of enquiries, the postholder will be expected to liaise effectively with colleagues across multiple departments and locations. The Reception and Appointment Clerk provides a frontline welcome, support, information and signposting to patients receiving treatment for cancer and those living with non-malignant blood conditions. The role is an integral part of the multidisciplinary team supporting both outpatient and day unit services Communication: o To welcome patients to the department, ensuring that patient information held is correct (address, telephone numbers, GP details, Next of Kin details), and that the attendance is recorded on Medway/Mosaiq. o To liaise with patients, wards, clinical staff, GPs and Trust support staff in person, via telephone and email as and when necessary. Patient Care: o To show a caring and professional approach towards patients, relatives and carers. This may require acting with resilience to deal with sometimes distressed patients and relatives in an empathetic manner Organising and Planning: o To carry out associated duties, for example, call handling, outcoming clinic appointments, booking bloods, managing the team inbox, scanning, and patient filing. Service Development and Research: o Attend training courses as required to support personal development and the needs of the service. o Assist in training of new members of the team. o To take part in departmental audits and associated duties. Finance and Resources: If and when appropriate and directed, order and/or receipt stationary and essential items, in line with Trust policies. Information Resources: o To book patient appointments in line with the Patient Access Policy, print letters and arrange any appointment related services as and when required (E.g. interpreting services). For a more detailed job description, main responsibilities, and Person Specification, please refer to the job description document attached to this vacancy.

title: Medical Secretary/Administrator
description: Greenway Community Practice is delighted to offer a rare opportunity to join our friendly, supportive and well-established team as an Medical Secretary/ Administrator. This is an ideal opportunity for an organised, enthusiastic and motivated individual looking to develop their career within primary care. The successful candidate will provide high-quality administrative and medical secretarial support to our clinical and administrative teams, helping to ensure the smooth and efficient running of the practice. You will provide a varied range of administrative and medical secretarial support, including managing clinical correspondence and referrals, supporting clinicians, processing workflow and accurately read-coding relevant information into patients electronic healthcare records. You will also provide administrative support to our wider multidisciplinary team and liaise with healthcare professionals and other organisations as required. More than anything, we value your energy and outlook - because we believe a positive, motivated team is key to delivering outstanding care. If youre looking to be part of a fun, dynamic team that genuinely enjoys working together, wed love to hear from you. The successful candidate will provide a high-quality medical secretarial service, supporting GPs and clinicians with the efficient management of patient-related administrative processes. Duties will include preparing and processing clinical correspondence, referrals, reports and other medical documentation. The post holder will be responsible for processing and tracking referrals, investigations and hospital correspondence, liaising with secondary care providers and other healthcare professionals where appropriate. The role will also involve monitoring and actioning incoming correspondence, scanning and filing clinical documents, allocating tasks to the appropriate clinician or team member, and following up outstanding actions where required. The post holder will ensure that confidential patient information is handled appropriately and in accordance with practice policies, information governance requirements and data protection legislation. In addition, the successful candidate will carry out workflow processes and accurately read-code relevant information into patients electronic healthcare records, in accordance with the practices coding policy and agreed procedures. Attention to detail and an understanding of medical terminology will be essential to ensure that clinical information is recorded accurately and consistently. Secretarial Opening Incoming post, internal and external, date stamp and circulate as appropriate. Sending outgoing post, internal and external, as required Typing GP referral letters and general correspondence, using eRs Typing Agendas and Minutes as required General typing, such as posters, leaflets, protocols etc., as required. Liaise with various hospital departments/secretaries regarding patient appointments/results/letters etc. as required. Use ICE to obtain results/clinic letters/appointment details etc. as required. Deal with patient enquiries regarding hospital appointments etc. Maintain the Private Fees Account, keeping a record of requests, responses, and payments in Deal with requests from Solicitors/Insurance Companies/Employers for Medical Reports, PMA Reports, copies of records etc.; prepare documentation as required; liaise with GPs to ensure a response; complete and send off. Deal with requests from Insurance Companies or individual patients for medicals; book appointments and liaise with GPs; sendoff reports. Deal with sundry and private fees payments coming in; enter on Private Fees Account and prepare regularly for banking. Devise protocols for secretarial duties Monitor the practice NHS.net email inbox throughout the day. Review and action incoming emails promptly. Forward emails to the appropriate staff member when required. Add patient-related emails to Docman for processing and filing

title: Practice Receptionist
description: West View Surgery are looking for a confident experienced part time receptionist to join our friendly team. Previous experience of working in a General Practice is preferred but not essential as full training will be given. This is a very busy and varied role, applicants must be able to multi-task, have a professional telephone manner and excellent computer skills. PLEASE APPLY USING THE ATTACHED APPLICATION FORM. Please note our reception shifts are 7.45am-1pm, and 1pm-6.30pm. The shift pattern for this role is currently 3 shifts per week, these will be on a Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Be able to offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice including the provision of clerical support to clinical staff Facilitate effective communication between patients, members the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Job description attached Opening up/locking-up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Taking messages and passing on information ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Filing, Scanning and retrieving paperwork Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers processing referrals to third parties/ secondary care

title: Medical Administrator
description: The Medical Administrator is responsible for providing comprehensive administrative support to the clinical and non-clinical teams within the GP practice. The post holder will ensure the accurate processing of patient information, maintain electronic medical records using SystmOne, and contribute to the efficient day-to-day running of the practice while delivering excellent patient care and customer service. Summarisation of electronic/Lloyd George patient record when received into the practice Entering of clinical information with relevant read coding onto patient records in SystmOne Scanning and read coding of patient clinical information Workflow to appropriate clinician Processing of SystmOne generated tasks such as Out of Hours reports, patient records to be merged etc. Processing of patient requests for online access to their detailed coded/full patient record to include redaction as necessary Dealing with electronic results Register new patients and process deductions in accordance with NHS guidelines. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records within SystmOne. Process changes to patient demographics and ensure records are updated promptly. Manage incoming and outgoing correspondence, including letters, emails and NHS communications. Scan, code and file clinical correspondence onto patient records using SystmOne. Handle requests for medical records in accordance with GDPR and NHS regulations. Process subject access requests and ensure confidentiality is maintained at all times. Use SystmOne effectively to manage patient records and administrative workflows. Code clinical information from hospital letters and other healthcare communications as directed. Process tasks and workflow items in a timely manner. Manage electronic document management systems, including scanning and workflow allocation. Support clinicians by maintaining accurate records and actioning administrative requests. Identify and report any system issues to management.
